items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated. Real gross domestic income (GDI) increased 4.4 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent (revised) in the second quarter. The average of real GDP and real GDI also increased 4.4 percent, compared with an increase of 2.2 percent (revised).

items.title: Fed survey shows continued economic growth, sticky inflation in recent weeks By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 25 (Reuters) - Economic growth persisted at a "slight to moderate" pace across most of the US in recent weeks, while inflation remained sticky and employment levels rose, a Federal Reserve survey showed on Wednesday, two weeks before central bank policymakers decide whether to raise interest rates. "Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior reporting period," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, health care, insurance, and tariff-related expenses." Still, input costs were outpacing selling price increases, suggesting growing pressure on corporate margins, the report said. "(C)ompetitive pressures and customer price sensitivity limited firms’ ability to fully pass through higher costs. Contacts expected both expenses and prices to continue rising in the coming months."

items.excerpt: EMBARGOED UNTIL RELEASE AT 8:30 a.m. EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026 Personal income increased $201.8 billion (0.7 percent at a monthly rate) in October, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $200.5 billion (0.8 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $63.8 billion (0.3 percent). Personal outlays—the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments—increased $69.3 billion in October. Personal saving was $1.00 trillion, and the personal saving rate—personal saving as a percentage of DPI—was 4.1 percent. The increase in current-dollar personal income in October primarily reflected increases in compensation, government social benefits, and personal income receipts on assets. The $63.8 billion increase in current-dollar PCE in October reflected increases of $11.8 billion in spending on goods and $52.1 billion in spending on services. Real PCE decreased $5.8 billion (less than 0.1 percent at a monthly rate) in October. From the preceding month, the PCE price index for October increased 0.3 percent. Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index also increased 0.3 percent. From the same month one year ago, the PCE price index for October increased 3.8 percent. items.title: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on goods from major U.S. trading partners : NPR
items.excerpt: KURTZLEBEN: Well, these are being implemented under a law known for short as Section 301, which is meant to counter other countries' unfair trade practices. And so here the White House is alleging that these other countries have what's called structural excess capacity in various manufactured goods. And the administration has described this as when another country has policies that cause a good to be overproduced, which then distorts a global market for that good. And so those practices, according to the administration, can include all sorts of things, like labor practices, subsidies and tax breaks. Now, the administration imposed other sweeping 301 tariffs earlier this year, and there's a lawsuit in process challenging those, with the key argument being that those tariffs were just way broader than the 301 law calls for. MARTÍNEZ: Now, you ... Could these new tariffs face similar legal challenges? KURTZLEBEN: You know, they could. We'll see what happens. But I talked to Sara Albrecht. She's chairman and CEO of the nonpartisan Liberty and Justice Center (ph), which filed that lawsuit against those earlier tariffs. And she said these new tariffs are not being used the way 301 tariffs are supposed to. SARA ALBRECHT: It is a negotiating tactic. That is not what tariffs, in a broad sense, are supposed to be. Like, you can do that on a country-by-country basis if they're addressing a specific problem, not just general, hey, we want better trade deals. KURTZLEBEN: In addition, both she and other trade experts say they think the White House is just proposing these new tariffs as a way to replace the sweeping tariffs the Supreme Court struck down earlier this year. MARTÍNEZ: Now, we all just found out how unpopular these tariffs were in the midterm elections. So how are these new tariffs landing politically? KURTZLEBEN: Well, we've heard some real pushback from congressional Democrats. Richard Neal, top House Democrat on the Ways and Means Committee, said in a statement, quote, "Trump is putting everything from family budgets to our national security at risk to keep his tariff scheme in place." Now, congressional Republicans have been quieter, and this does come a few weeks after they lost dozens of seats in the election, which is widely attributed, in large part, to high prices, and tariffs do cause higher prices.

items.excerpt: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65 Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of Duran Duran, has died at 65. The band was known for hits like “Hungry Like the Wolf” and “Rio.” Taylor revealed his battle with Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2022. Duran Duran's rise was linked to MTV, and they became icons of the 1980s. Their success included two Grammy Awards, nine gold records, and six platinum ones. Taylor's guitar style helped define the band's sound. Despite internal struggles, Duran Duran's impact on music and pop culture remains significant. Taylor's legacy continues with his recent solo album release. ... French actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on rape charge, lawyer says PARIS (AP) — A lawyer representing French actor Gérard Depardieu says he has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping a young actress at his Paris home in 2018. Defense lawyer Delphine Meillet told the Associated Press in a written message Thursday that the 77-year-old actor would face trial over only one of two alleged rapes reported by actress Charlotte Arnould. Depardieu has denied the allegations. The development comes less than two weeks after Depardieu abandoned his appeal against a sexual assault conviction in a separate case. He was convicted in May 2025 of groping two women on a film set in 2021. The cases have put one of French cinema’s most celebrated figures at the center of the country’s #MeToo reckoning. Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt settle winery fight lawsuit that surfaced abuse allegations LOS ANGELES (AP) — Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt have settled their long-running legal battles over a French winery. In a joint statement Wednesday, they announced the settlement, saying it's in the best interests of their family. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016, alleging Pitt abused her and their children during a flight. The FBI investigated but didn't pursue charges. The winery lawsuit revealed more details of the abuse allegations and their split, with Pitt accusing Jolie of selling her share without his consent. Both actors have remained private about their breakup, focusing on their careers and family. Gordon Ramsay to take the lead in revival of BBC's flagship motoring program 'Top Gear' LONDON (AP) — Gordon Ramsay, the renowned British chef and restaurateur who has forged a successful career on television, will lead the revival of the BBC’s motoring program “Top Gear.” Ramsay, whose hit shows on both sides of the Atlantic include “Hell’s Kitchen” and “Ramsay’s Kitchen Nightmares,” said Wednesday that he “can’t wait to get started.” Filming will take place across the U.K., including at the show’s Dunsfold Aerodrome base southwest of London and around the world next year, for broadcast in 2028. “Top Gear” has been off air since 2022 when former cricketer Andrew Flintoff was seriously injured, during filming.
